counterfactual_missing_items: Histologic or orchiectomy tissue confirmation is not provided
AFP and hCG are normal, so a germ-cell-marker signature is not demonstrated
The lesion is characterized only by imaging; no staging or pathologic sampling is provided
decisive_items: a 1.09 × 0.79 cm well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow
the left testis was enlarged, firm, smooth, without discrete nodules or tenderness
left testicular bloating and dull pain
response.rationale: R4 is the only candidate whose raw spans directly support an intratesticular vascular solid lesion with a firm enlarged testis, making testicular cancer the most likely diagnosis. The epididymal cysts and hydrocele are incidental secondary findings, and torsion is contradicted by the chronic 20-year course, absence of tenderness, and internal Doppler flow. C1 is an append-only completion of R4 with no independent raw support, so it is treated as a correlated restatement.

rejected.why: Append-only completion of R4; raw spans are subsets of R4 and add no independent evidence.
Bilateral epididymal cysts are incidental small findings and do not explain the intratesticular hypoechoic lesion.
A small hydrocele is only a secondary fluid collection and cannot explain the solid left testicular mass.
Torsion is contradicted by chronicity, lack of tenderness, and internal blood flow on Doppler.
